host.description: Azure F16as_v6, AMD EPYC 9V74 (virtualized), 16 vCPU = 16 cores (no SMT), 64 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17.0-azure. Shards and Redis processes on cpus 8-15, one redis-benchmark per shard on cpus 0-7, loopback. Ruvio memory durability, Redis without AOF or RDB.

build.ruvio_commit: per-shard forwarding branch (claude/project-thread-dd1fzw) with the lean dispatch path enabled in per-shard mode
build.redis: Redis 8.10.2 built from source (jemalloc 5.3.0); redis-benchmark and redis-cli from the same build

redis_version: Redis server v=8.10.2 sha=498ecd0d:0 malloc=jemalloc-5.3.0 bits=64 build=a79b1be71986fe56

config.method: one redis-benchmark per shard on its own port with keys in a hash tag that shard owns; rates summed over shards

rows.label: LPOS (100 elements, hit in the middle)
BITFIELD INCRBY u8 (always writes)
rows.note: Redis refuses zero-padded offsets, so the offset is fixed

rows.label: DUMP (64 B string)
rows.note: formats differ: Ruvio's is not RDB

rows.label: GEOSEARCH (radius 50 km, COUNT 10)
rows.note: all points share one coordinate: worst case

rows.label: GETEX (set a 100 s deadline)
rows.note: Ruvio's GETEX takes milliseconds only; each side uses its own syntax

notes.memory: memory table from the first run of the same day (binary before the lean-path change, which does not touch memory)
notes.one_shard_control: rows of one Ruvio shard against one Redis on cpu 8 with the client on cpus 2,3
notes.publish: PUBLISH fans out to every shard through the forwarding fabric and waits for the replies; Redis Cluster broadcasts it asynchronously
